The theorem uses within-output Lipschitz smoothness; no injective representation or shared-label hypothesis is imposed.

Eq.(7) reads1>0 while its claimed cross-sample gradient bound would give2<=0. Solving 4(W-1)+epsilon W=0 gives4/(4+epsilon); test loss increases for all epsilon>0 and derivative at0=1/4. With test label0, the surrogate decreases but additive attention output1+1=2 raises .5F^2 from.5 to2. For h=3,label0, criterion1>8 fails yet surrogate4/(4+9epsilon) decreases test loss.
P1.alternatives_boundaries: The cross-label example is excluded by a genuinely stronger common-gradient/cross-sample regularity hypothesis; the report states that limitation. Positive gradient sign, Hessian preconditioning and finite Taylor remainder are distinct issues. No finite-example effect on real LLM scores is inferred.
